evals.name: designs a replenishment program timed to the observed cycle
evals.prompt: We sell dog food in 5lb and 15lb bags. Retention-diagnosis says our leak is first-time buyers who never place a second order. Build me a replenishment reminder program.
expect: times the first reminder to 70-80% of the observed per-SKU cycle from the brand's own inter-purchase data, adjusted for bag size and quantity, and treats the label as a starting assumption
specifies each touch with purpose, timing + rationale, channel, job, proof element, CTA, and anti-goal, with a one-tap prefilled reorder as the CTA and no finished copy
includes exits for reorder in any channel, subscription start, and suppression after a larger-size purchase, plus a graduation branch to subscription after 2-3 on-time reorders
states on-time repeat rate as the primary KPI, a customer-level sticky holdout, and a dated kill condition in the SKILL.md output
labels every benchmark number [Assumption] and hands customers far past their cycle to winback-series

evals.name: refuses replenishment for a non-consumable catalog
evals.prompt: We sell sofas and dining tables. Set up a replenishment reminder flow so customers come back every 90 days.
expect: says plainly that the catalog is not consumable and has no usage cycle to time reminders against
declines to invent a replenishment cadence
routes to post-purchase or loyalty-program, and to retention-diagnosis if the leak is unknown

evals.name: refuses to design without a known leak
evals.prompt: Retention feels bad. Just build us a replenishment program, we don't have cohort data handy.
expect: routes to retention-diagnosis first because the leak zone is unknown
does not produce a full program blueprint designed in the dark
offers to proceed with directional inputs labeled [Assumption] once the leak is located

evals.name: avoids the label-timing, discount, and no-holdout traps
evals.prompt: Our vitamins are a 30-day supply, so send the reminder at day 25 with 20% off, include subscribers so they don't miss it, and we'll call every reorder after the email a win.
expect: replaces label timing with the observed median inter-purchase interval, adjusted for quantity, and flags day 25 as an [Assumption] until the data confirms it
removes the default discount and explains it gives margin to customers who would reorder anyway
requires a holdout and refuses to claim reorders after a send as lift
does not write subject lines or body copy and never sends anything
